briefFidelity: FAIL, and the failure is the brief's own central sentence. The brief demands 'an all-over field rather than a figure on a ground' with 'no single dominant element.' Before reading it, I described every one of the twelve as 'a single centred island floating in a wide empty margin, never touching or crossing an edge, so every token is a vignette with a lot of dead ground around it.' That is a figure on a ground, verbatim, arrived at blind. The marks never reach the frame; the empty perimeter is what defines the mass as an object, and an object is precisely what an interval study must not produce. Three tokens (9369, 9548, 10801) go further and fail the second clause too: their large squares fuse into one pale slab that IS the whole token, a single dominant element with no interval left to read, and at 512px that slab acquires a nameable subject -- a stack of translucent sheets or cards -- against the brief's 'nothing should invite a viewer to name it.' The palette clause is met (narrow, tonal, monochrome, no hue) and the 'tokens differ in count and placement' clause is met, but those are the satisfiable parts of the brief, not its thesis. What was asked for was spacing as the only content; what was made is a centred figure whose spacing is internal decoration.
seedVariation: Real but coarse, and it collapses at browse size. At 256px there are genuinely different works here -- ruled grids (9011, 9906, 10980), dense scatters (9727, 10085, 10264, 10622), fused stacks (9369, 9548, 10801), a near-empty sprinkle (10443), a small curled cluster (9190). At 120px that resolves to four or five distinguishable kinds, not twelve: the three fused stacks are close to interchangeable pale lumps, and the grids differ mainly in row count. Shared identity is not the problem; the problem is that the identity is carried by the archetype rather than by the interval, so within an archetype the seeds stop separating.
thumbnailSurvival: It reads, but only as a value mass. Archetype and overall density survive; the square/diamond alternation, the individual rotations and every overlap seam are gone. 10443 nearly disappears into a faint sprinkle. The fused stacks survive as a featureless blob, which is survival of the silhouette but not of the work -- an interval study whose intervals are invisible at browse size has not survived, it has been replaced by its outline.
marketResponse: Visible, and roughly the change claimed -- but the mechanism drifts from density to structure. Density does move and moves legibly: 9011 drops from seven columns to five under stress and returns denser and creamier in recovery, which reads at 120px. But in the large-square tokens the dominant stress event is not thinning, it is a CLEAVE -- 9369 tears into a top and bottom half with a dark gap, 9190 separates into two clusters, 9548 has a bite taken out of its lower edge. A tear is a figural event, not a density event, and it makes the object more object-like under stress rather than dissolving the field. So the transformation is visible and is not fabricated, but in the tokens that most need it, it works against the brief instead of for it.
tokenIdentity: Holds. 9011 is a grid in all three conditions, 9369 a pale slab, 9190 a small curled cluster, 9548 a squarish mass. No token becomes a different work under stress or recovery.
composition: Clean execution, no clipping, no rendering artifacts, no mush in the scatter and grid tokens. The failure is compositional intent rather than craft: uniform centre-weighting across all twelve, a wide unused margin in every frame, and no edge tension anywhere. Focal hierarchy is inverted from what was asked -- the brief wanted none, and the fused stacks supply a single overwhelming focus while the grids supply an even field the margin then reframes as an object.
reasoning: I wrote, without having seen the brief, that every token is a centred island in a wide empty margin that never touches an edge; the brief then turned out to ask for the exact opposite in its second sentence, an all-over field rather than a figure on a ground, with no single dominant element. That is not a matter of degree or of taste -- it is the one formal instruction the brief is most specific about, and the work reads as its negation in all twelve seeds, most severely in the three tokens whose large translucent squares fuse into one nameable pale slab. The palette is right, the seed variation is real, and the market transformation is genuinely visible, so this is competent work that would be defensible under a different brief; but the gate is fidelity, the gate fails, and this is a permanent on-chain commitment.
wouldChange: Let the field run to and through the frame. Remove the centred island and the dead margin -- distribute marks edge to edge and let them be cropped by the boundary, so the frame is a window onto a continuing field rather than a stage holding an object. In the same pass, cap the mark scale so no token can fuse into one dominant mass: the three large-square stacks have no interval left to read at any size, which is the failure of the brief's actual subject.
